good_form.point: Follow through fully, finishing high over the opposite shoulder with the racket tip up, then release and recover.
Turn the shoulders (and hips less than shoulders) fully, until the front shoulder is under the chin, so the body powers the shot.
Keep the grip and wrists relaxed, so the racket can drop under the ball and accelerate.
Let the racket drop below the ball, then swing low to high to a contact point out in front.
Use the non-dominant hand as the leading, swinging hand, with the bottom hand only stabilizing.
Stay low and athletic with bent legs, and transfer weight forward through the ball.
Start turning the shoulders early, as the ball leaves the opponent's strings, and finish the preparation by the bounce.
Keep space between the elbows and the body in preparation and contact, not tucked in.
Power the swing from the ground up through the legs, hips and trunk, not the arms.
Step forward into the ball and get behind it, with the head steady and still until after contact.
Shorten the preparation on fast balls or returns.
Move the non-dominant arm back as the hitting arm goes forward, to stay aligned and balanced and avoid over-rotating.
Keep the racket on the hitting side of the hands through contact so the strings face the target longer.
Hit the ball high over the net for margin, spin and depth.

faults.description: Squeezing the racket or tensing the wrists so the racket cannot drop and accelerate freely.

causes.cause: Tension in the hands and small wrist muscles
Focusing on small muscles instead of the big body muscles

fixes.idea: Relax the hands; use roughly 3 out of 10 grip pressure.
Imagine throwing the racket head and letting the arms follow.
Keep the hand relaxed so the racket accelerates in a slapping motion.
Consciously use the legs, core, hips and shoulders and keep the wrist relaxed.
Practice with a cut-down preparation to force acceleration from a relaxed hand.

outcome_effects: Racket cannot get under the ball
Less racket head speed, spin, power and angles

faults.description: The takeback is too high, too long, a straight down-and-back line, or has a straight hitting arm.

causes.cause: Top arm flaring out like a chicken wing
Non-dominant hand far from the body, straightening the hitting arm
Closed stance allowing a very long backswing
Down-and-back is easier for newer players

fixes.idea: Drop the elbow toward the rib cage and dip the racket as if into a pool.
Use a loop or C shape: head above the hands, drop below the ball, pull up and forward.
Keep the non-dominant hand close to the body so the hitting arm bends.
Use an open stance and keep the preparation short.

outcome_effects: Slapping at or hitting down on the ball, missing in the net
faults.disagreement: Source 0 wants the racket head above the hands at the start of the loop, source 2 wants a low takeback, and source 10 wants the racket head up; a down-and-back takeback is a fault for source 0 but acceptable on returns.

faults.description: Pulling the racket across the body instead of extending through the ball to a high finish.

causes.cause: Bottom hand driving the swing
Bending the elbows before the left arm extends
Already extended on the front leg with no room to go forward
Non-hitting arm hanging

fixes.idea: Let the top hand do all the swinging, with only a light bottom-hand hold.
Let the off arm dictate the extension; bend the elbows only once it is fairly straight.
Transfer weight forward and hold a definite finish.
Finish high with the elbow and butt cap pointing at the opponent.

outcome_effects: Lack of depth and missing wide
Balls into the net, less topspin

faults.description: Generating power with the arms rather than the legs, hips and trunk.

causes.cause: Trying to hit harder with the arms because both hands are on the racket
Short, rushed contact
Not using body weight and legs

fixes.idea: Shift weight forward, drive off the front leg and rotate hips and trunk.
Push into the ground and let the energy flow up through the body.
Pull-rope drill with a rope fixed below hip height on a fence to engage the whole body.
Slow the motion down and hold the ball on the strings.

faults.description: Waiting for, preparing and hitting with the elbows jammed against the body or hip.

causes.cause: Ball coming right at the body with no space
Focusing on the right elbow and finish while neglecting the left elbow
Waiting for the ball with the arms tucked in

fixes.idea: Move the left elbow away from the body on takeback, with a gap as on a forehand.
Start with the arms out, split step, then rotate while keeping the spacing.
Do the step-back drill, jumping backward and sideways to make space.
Practice one-handed left-handed forehands with the top hand.

faults.description: Breaking, scooping or casting the wrist so the racket rolls over, instead of guiding through with the hands and arms.

causes.cause: Left wrist casting over and wrists flying after contact
Right hand slipped to bevel 3, leaving the wrist too loose
Not thinking of the left palm going to the target

fixes.idea: Imagine hitting with the left palm to the target, then release at the end.
Keep the racket on the hitting side of the hands as you lift.
Return the right hand to bevel 2.
Let the hands follow through with the arms.

outcome_effects: Strings point down and change direction
Left arm cannot guide the ball

faults.description: Starting the turn and preparation only after the ball has crossed the net or bounced.

causes.cause: Waiting to turn until the ball crosses the net or bounces

fixes.idea: Start turning the shoulders the instant the ball leaves the opponent's strings.
Have the preparation finished when the ball bounces, so the bounce is the cue to accelerate.
Turn the shoulders first on fast balls and get the shoulder under the chin early.

outcome_effects: Contact too far back with weight going backward

faults.description: The non-dominant arm hangs or stays in place instead of moving back as the hitting arm goes forward or leading the extension.

causes.cause: Playing only with the hitting arm

fixes.idea: Swing the non-dominant arm back as the hitting arm goes forward, opening the chest.
Hold the finish with the arm behind.
Keep shoulders aligned with the ball, including down the line.

outcome_effects: Loss of ball control and shanked balls

faults.description: Hands on the wrong bevels or slid too far, which weakens the wrist and blocks the swing.

causes.cause: Top hand rotated too far over, or bottom hand not Continental or Eastern
Sliding the hand too far from the forehand grip

fixes.idea: Put the top hand back on its correct bevel with knuckle-to-palm on the bevel.
Keep the knuckle on the edge of the bevel for the Eastern backhand.
Beginners can hold the racket under the armpit and pull it out like a sword to find the grip.

outcome_effects: No power or swing, so the racket is pulled across
Cannot get under or maneuver the ball
Shot feels like a baseball swing
faults.disagreement: The sources recommend different grips: left bevel 7 and right bevel 2 (3); bottom Continental or Eastern, top Eastern (4); dominant Eastern or semi-western, non-dominant Continental (5); dominant Continental, non-dominant mild Eastern or semi-western (11).

faults.description: Not turning the shoulders enough, or turning hips and shoulders as one block, or just poking the ball.

causes.cause: Turning the hips as much as the shoulders, with no gap
Beginners just wanting to get the ball back

fixes.idea: Turn until the front shoulder touches the chin.
Do the mirror drill, turning fully with the eyes fixed on your own eyes.
Turn the hips less than the shoulders, like pulling a bowstring.
Turn, prep and step into the shot.

faults.description: Stepping out on wide balls, or stopping after the shot, so you are not ready for the next ball.

causes.cause: Moving the legs out rather than rotating on wide balls
Assuming the shot is a winner

fixes.idea: Rotate out through the legs and push off the front leg to recover to the middle.
Always recover after every shot.

outcome_effects: Caught out if the ball returns

faults.description: Stopping or checking the swing after contact, with the elbow tucked and the racket not finishing up.

causes.cause: Stopping the swing when the ball leaves the strings
Elbow tucked into the body after contact
Not lifting enough through the swing

fixes.idea: Go through the ball and continue all the way up, finishing over the opposite shoulder.
Finish with the racket tip pointing at the sky, or the butt cap forward.
Imagine a volleyball under the armpit.

outcome_effects: Loss of spin, direction and power

faults.description: Standing tall on the front leg, with the back leg straight or the head and body popping up, so there is little weight transfer.

causes.cause: Head coming up early, bringing the body up
Being on the front leg before the swing starts
Straight back leg locking the hip
Not getting low with the legs

fixes.idea: Get low with bent legs and the front heel down.
Spread weight evenly on both legs, then transfer forward in a U shape.
Bend the back leg more to free the hip.
Keep the head down until contact and visualize the contact point in front.
Use a side or crossover step to reach farther balls.

outcome_effects: Mistimed balls, ball goes up or sprays
Short contact and hitting across the body

faults.description: A left-eye dominant player uses right-eye footwork, so the dominant eye faces sideways.

causes.cause: Using the right-eye-dominant footwork pattern

fixes.idea: Land on the left leg so the dominant eye faces the court.
Use an open stance if short on time.

outcome_effects: Poor view of the ball and court

faults.description: The ball goes over the net flat and direct instead of high and loopy.

fixes.idea: Hit a loopy ball that goes high over the net.

outcome_effects: Lack of the high, loopy shape wanted

faults.description: Waiting for a high-bouncing ball and hitting it over the shoulder.

causes.cause: Waiting for the ball to drop instead of taking it early

fixes.idea: Step in and take the ball early on the rise.
Mix in slice or flat shots.

outcome_effects: Short replies that can be attacked

faults.description: Lifting the ball with the arm instead of letting the racket head swing around the hand.

causes.cause: Trying to lift the ball with the arm

fixes.idea: Finish high, with the racket head going around the hand after the low-to-high body move.

faults.description: Rushing forward or stretching for the ball instead of letting it come.

causes.cause: Not trusting there is enough time

fixes.idea: Let the ball come to you and stay calm.
Get closer to the ball with the legs.

faults.description: Stepping across the body and getting jammed so you cannot swing.

causes.cause: Stepping across instead of getting behind the ball

fixes.idea: Step out and then in, forward to the ball.
Get behind the ball.
